13th Place Solution — NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge
NVIDIA Nemotron Model Reasoning Challenge


Solution Writeup · 13th place · Jun 19, 2026
First, I would like to sincerely thank the organizers for hosting such an insightful and educational
competition. I also greatly appreciate the Kaggle community for sharing valuable discussions
and open-source code, which were highly informative throughout the competition. My approach
focused primarily on training data construction and iterative refinement. Special thanks to
@huikang for releasing a highly polished and well-designed dataset generation pipeline in the
Open Progress Prize Publication, which served as the foundation of my approach.

Overview & Key Approach
To improve the accuracy of teacher-generated Chain-of-Thought (CoT) traces, I built upon the
reasoners released in the Open Progress Prize Publication and introduced several task-specific
heuristics that increased the proportion of correctly solved training examples.

Performance Summary

TOTAL                   8,496 9,500 89.4%

Note: Overall accuracy increased from 87.7% to 89.4%, with major
improvements achieved in equation_numeric_guess, equation_numeric_deduce,
and bit_manipulation.

Reasoner Modifications by Category
1. bit_manipulation

Key Enhancements

   •   Added explicit verification of 3-input operations, specifically MAJORITY and XNOR.
   •   Restricted the search space using inferred input bit-position information derived from the
       left and right operands.
   •   Implemented left-edge propagation as the default fallback rule when no valid operation
       was found.
   •   Removed the parsing-display section to free token budget for the additional verification
       process.

2. cryptarithm

Output Format Simplification

Reduced syntax ambiguity caused by extra braces appearing in final answers:

   •   Old: output: 【%&$>】 -> 【{%&$>}】
   •   New: output: 【%&$>】

Robust Aggregation

After parsing both the examples and the target problem, the solver collects statistics on usage
patterns of the target operator (e.g., consistency with concatenation or reverse concatenation). To
mitigate symbol transcription errors, an operation is treated as a valid candidate if it matches at
least one relevant example, rather than requiring strict consistency across all examples.

Fallback Strategy

When examples using the target operator are available, the solver evaluates both concatenation
and reverse concatenation.
If neither yields a unique solution:

   1. Collect all symbols.
   2. Identify operator symbols vs. non-operator symbols.
   3. Return the first remaining non-operator symbol as the final answer.
      This removes logical contradictions where concatenation was incorrectly applied to tasks
      for which the examples already demonstrated that it was inappropriate.

Dataset Rebalancing & Augmentation

Fallback-type tasks were heavily overrepresented in the data. I rebalanced the training set so that
tasks solved correctly versus incorrectly by the teacher model maintained a 1:1 ratio. To offset
the reduction in data volume, I used equation_numeric as seeds to generate new tasks, increasing
the total number of cryptarithm training samples by approximately 3x.

3. equation_numeric

The solver was fundamentally redesigned around strong structural assumptions regarding
operator behavior.

My Hypotheses

   1. Operator Categorization Operator functions belong to four mutually exclusive
      categories:
          o Addition category: add, add-1, add+1
          o Multiplication category: mul, mul-1, mul+1
          o Subtraction category: subtraction, absolute difference, reverse subtraction,
              negated absolute difference, max mod min
          o Concatenation category: concatenation, reverse concatenation
   2. Exclusivity Different operator symbols cannot belong to the same functional category.
   3. Symmetry Reverse transformation applies to either both inputs and outputs or neither.
      This rule is shared across all examples within the same task.

Implemented Enhancements

   •   Determined the global reversal rule via majority voting across all available examples.
   •   Target Operator Identification
   •   For Deduce Tasks: Verified candidate functions using only target-operator examples
       under the inferred reverse-transformation rule.
   •   For Guess Tasks: Evaluated all examples under the inferred rule, identified operator
       families already assigned to other symbols, and strictly selected a non-overlapping family
       for the target operator. If multiple candidates remained, ties were resolved via:
       subtraction > addition > multiplication > concatenation.

Target Operator Identification for Guess Tasks Example

Select fallback function for the question operator
Function category mapping:
  difference-type: subtraction, absolute difference, negated absolute
difference, reverse subtraction, max mod min
  addition-type: addition, add+1, add-1
  multiplication-type: multiplication, multiply+1, multiply-1
  concatenation-type: concatenation, reverse concatenation
Predefined fallback functions (priority order): subtraction (a-b), addition,
multiplication, concatenation
Function identified from the examples: multiplication, subtraction (a-b).
Fallback function category (priority order): difference-type, addition-type,
multiplication-type, concatenation-type
Function category identified from the examples: multiplication-type,
difference-type
Unused fallback function category (priority order): addition-type,
concatenation-type
Selected fallback category: addition-type

Model Training (SFT Strategy)
Using the newly engineered dataset, I performed Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) using Unsloth.
Special thanks to @konbu17 for sharing the original notebook and to @dgxchen for publishing
an improved version, which I further adapted for my experiments.
Since the primary objective was to improve Chain-of-Thought (CoT) trace generation and reduce
trace-level reasoning errors (rather than improve generalized zero-shot reasoning), I intentionally
adopted an aggressive, overfitting-prone setup and utilized the entire constructed dataset across
three stages of SFT.

LoRA Adapter Configuration

   •     Rank / Alpha: 32 / 32 (Dropout: 0)
   •     Target Modules: q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, in_proj, out_proj,
         up_proj, down_proj

3-Stage SFT Schedule

          Data        Learning
Stage          Epochs          Scheduler                         Notes / Strategy
          Size          Rate
1st
         9,277   2      2.0e-4       Linear     Initial alignment on the core clean traces.
SFT
2nd                                             Further fine-tuning and smoothing the loss
         9,277   1      2.0e-5       Cosine
SFT                                             surface.
3rd                                             Upsampled bit_manipulation and cryptarithm
         11,315 1       5.0e-6       Cosine
SFT                                             examples to address residual trace errors.

Effective batch size of 32 and the AdamW optimizer were used consistently across
all three stages.
